text: We are viewing the flat on rue Victor-Hugo.
Many people view the same flat.
I viewed three flats this week.
My sister viewed the flat yesterday.
You will view the flat on Thursday. (formal)
I will view it with my guarantor.
When we lived in Lyon, we used to view flats every Saturday.
I was viewing the flat when the agent called.
I ask for a café crème every morning.
If you ask for 'un café', they'll serve you an espresso. (formal)
Are the customers asking for the bill?
This morning I asked for a croissant with my coffee.
The waitress asked us to wait.
Did you ask for the bill? (informal)
Nobody will ask you to leave. (formal)
We will ask for a table on the terrace.
When you lived in Paris, you used to ask for a café crème at the counter. (informal)
We were asking for the bill when it started to rain.
I receive my salary at the end of the month.
The adviser sees clients by appointment.
Do you receive your salary in France? (formal)
We received our bank cards this morning.
They received an electricity bill yesterday. (male)
You will receive your card in a week's time. (formal)
She will receive an answer from the bank on Monday.
When I was a student, I used to receive a grant every month.
My parents used to receive their bills by post.
We give our carte Vitale at the surgery.
Are you giving me a prescription? (formal)
The doctor gave me a prescription yesterday.
Did you give your carte Vitale to the doctor? (informal)
This morning I gave my phone number to the surgery.
The doctor will give you a prescription. (formal)
They will give us the results on Friday. (male)
When we were children, our mother used to give us honey for a cold.
You were giving your name when the doctor arrived. (informal)
We book our TGV tickets in advance.
Most travellers book their ticket on their phone.
Do you book your tickets online? (formal)
I booked my ticket yesterday evening.
My brother booked a seat on the TGV to Marseille.
You will book your return journey on the website. (formal)
They will book their seats tomorrow. (male)
When she was a student, she used to book the cheapest seats.
You were booking your ticket when the train filled up. (informal)
I'm helping the elderly lady carry her bags.
We help the customers in the shop.
Did you help the old man in the lift? (informal)
The children helped their grandmother this morning.
The baker helped my son yesterday.
I will help you choose, madam.
Our neighbours will help us on Saturday.
When you worked in the shop, you used to help the older customers. (formal)
He was helping a stranger when I came into the bakery.
The stallholder serves the customers one by one.
We serve local cheese on our stall.
I served thirty customers this morning.
The cheese seller served my mother before me.
Did you serve the man with the basket? (informal)
I'll serve you in five minutes, madam.
The stallholders will serve soup at the end of the market.
When you had a stall, you used to serve the best tomatoes in town. (formal)
You were serving a customer when I arrived. (informal)
I'm bringing all my documents to the town hall.
Lots of people bring too many documents.
Do you always bring photocopies to the counter? (formal)
I brought my passport this morning.
My husband brought the form yesterday.
You will bring your son's birth certificate. (formal)
We will bring the file next Monday.
Before the internet, people used to bring every form to the town hall.
I was bringing my file to the counter when the clerk called me.
We live on the third floor of an old building.
In French cities, lots of people live in flats.
Do you live in this building? (formal)
I lived next to a very noisy neighbour for two years.
The caretaker lived in the building for thirty years.
Have you ever lived in a block of flats? (informal)
Next year, they will live in a building with a caretaker. (male)
You will live on the ground floor, next to the caretaker. (formal)
When I was twenty, I used to live in a tiny flat in Paris.
In the past, a caretaker used to live in every building.
We start work at nine o'clock.
New employees often start their day at reception.
Do you start by saying "vous" to your colleagues? (formal)
I started my new job on Monday.
My manager started the meeting at ten o'clock.
Tomorrow, the new colleague will start in the open-plan office.
I will start by introducing myself to the team.
When I worked in Lyon, I used to start at eight o'clock.
We were starting the meeting when the new colleague arrived.
